comparison: Both strongly support the morphological measurements of human vs mouse PCs (C11-C33). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative detail and internal consistency; peer reviewers call it 'exceptionally detailed' and 'convincing.' Both also address C2-C4, C94-C95, C131 regarding PC size comparisons, with complete agreement on the quality and validity of the data.

Both support spine morphology findings (C34-C50). OpenEval notes the data is quantitatively supported but acknowledges diffraction limit concerns for absolute measurements. Peer reviewers describe 'meticulous quantification' and 'interesting and unexpected new findings' without raising methodological concerns about the spine measurements.

Both support the novel spine structure findings (C7, C51-C57). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes imaging resolution limitations and speculative functional significance. Peer reviewers affirm the finding as 'interesting and unexpected' without questioning validity, accepting the younger tissue control for age-related concerns.

Major disagreement on climbing fiber multi-innervation (C58-C63). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to sparse labeling (44 PCs), ambiguous classification, and methodological limitations. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, explicitly affirming the findings and calling the CF labeling results 'important' without raising concerns about sample size or methodology.

Both support regional demographic and clustering findings (C64-C74). OpenEval emphasizes methodological soundness of statistical controls and spatial analysis. Peer reviewers affirm 'systematic and thorough methodology' and 'meticulous quantification.' Peer result also includes C9-C10, C75-C77, C107-C112, C135-C138 on regional variation and functional correlations, all supported.

OpenEval addresses regional morphology variation (C75-C77, C9-C10) as supported, noting correlation with functional boundaries. This overlaps with peer R5 which includes these claims in a broader supported evaluation of regional and clustering findings.

Both support claims about human PCs as largest neurons (C2-C3, C94-C95, C131). OpenEval notes substantial size differences and reliance on literature values for pyramidal cells. Peer reviewers include these claims in their overall affirmation of morphological findings without specific concerns.

Both address synaptic input extrapolation (C8, C96-C97). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with detailed mathematical validation. Peer reviewers include C8 in their supported evaluation of CF multi-innervation findings, affirming the input calculations without methodological concerns.

Partial overlap on interpretive claims. OpenEval addresses C4, C86-C88 as SUPPORTED (conserved/divergent features, 'differ in kind' inference). Peer R6 rates C86-C91, C98-C106 as UNCERTAIN, noting functional implications are 'by necessity, purely anatomical' and require validation. Agreement that anatomical observations are solid but functional interpretations are speculative.

Strong agreement on speculative functional claims (C89-C91, C99-C103). Both rate UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes these are 'explicitly speculative interpretations' lacking direct validation. Peer reviewers state functional differences 'remain to be seen' and acknowledge these as hypotheses requiring future testing.

OpenEval addresses morphology-function framework (C107-C109, C112-C113) as SUPPORTED, noting correlative nature. Peer R5 includes C107-C112 in broader supported evaluation of regional/clustering findings. However, C113 (novelty claim) is addressed separately in peer R9 as UNCERTAIN.

OpenEval rates C113 (novelty of morphological clustering) as SUPPORTED based on literature review. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting they do not explicitly evaluate whether this phenomenon is truly unprecedented or cerebellum-specific.

Both support literature-based contextual claims (C78-C85). OpenEval notes these are appropriately cited established knowledge. Peer reviewers accept these background statements without challenge, implicitly affirming the characterization of prior work.

Both support literature summary claims (C92-C93). OpenEval notes appropriate citations and well-documented comparisons. Peer reviewers include these in accepted background context, acknowledging the current work 'surpasses any prior publication.'

OpenEval addresses cautionary literature citations (C104-C106) as SUPPORTED contextual notes. Peer R6 includes these claims in UNCERTAIN evaluation of functional interpretations, using them to support the view that functional implications require validation.

Perfect agreement on introductory/background claims (C114-C130). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are appropriately cited established knowledge. Peer reviewers accept all background statements without challenge, acknowledging prior work as valid context.

OpenEval addresses preview statements (C132-C138) as SUPPORTED, noting they summarize findings detailed in results. Peer R2 includes C132 in supported spine findings evaluation. Other preview claims (C133-C138) appear in peer R3, R4, and R5 as part of supported evaluations.
OpenEval rates C132-C138 preview statements as SUPPORTED. Peer R3 includes C133 in supported evaluation of novel spine structure findings.
